w: Also called Li Galli, the Cocks, this archipelago of small islands sits between Capri and Positano, 6 km off the Amalfi Coast, administratively attached to Positano. Ancient legend places the mythological sirens here, whose song was said to lure sailors onto the rocks; the name Sirenuse comes from that story.
s: Islands named for the sirens said to haunt them

w: Officially the Cathedral of Saints Philip and James, Sorrento's Duomo stands on Via Santa Maria della Pieta and has anchored the town's religious life for centuries. It served as seat of the bishops and archbishops of Sorrento before the diocese merged in 1986 into the Archdiocese of Sorrento-Castellammare di Stabia.

w: The largest of the three Li Galli islands, Gallo Lungo curves like a sickle, or a leaping dolphin, its concave side sheltering a bay behind La Castelluccia and La Rotonda. A small cove called la Praja lets boats anchor off a short beach, beside a single house. On its barren summit stands an old watchtower.
s: Sickle-shaped island with a watchtower at its summit

w: This active lighthouse stands at the very tip of the Sorrentine Peninsula, the rocky spur separating the Bay of Naples from the Amalfi Coast. Marking Punta Campanella, the peninsula's south-western extremity, it has guided ships along the Tyrrhenian Sea for generations, a fixed point between two coasts.
s: Lighthouse at the tip of the Sorrentine Peninsula
_facts: Located at the south-western extremity of the Sorrentine Peninsula
